name: Sable Station
headline: Sable Station (financed as 15 Sable Apartments) is a 154-home, four-story affordable building for households at or below 70% AMI at 14455 E. Ellsworth Ave. in Aurora, on land bought from RTD near Aurora City Center, developed by DBG Properties with Featherstone Development; it won $2,197,931 a year in 2022 federal 4% credit with $24.9M of CHFA bonds and is now leasing.
why_it_matters: A transit-oriented 4% deal on land bought from RTD that pairs a property tax abatement partnership with the Aurora Housing Authority and a single private-placement construction-to-permanent loan, a stack other suburban developers can copy.

status.label: Open and leasing; no certificate of occupancy record found; 8609s not yet issued
status.detail: Aurora issued the building permit on 2023-04-10; a wall sign permit for Sable Station Apts was issued in February 2026 and Mission Rock Residential markets units as ready now (viewed 2026-10-21). Aurora's 2023 to 2026 certificate of occupancy layers have no entry for 14455 E Ellsworth Ave, and CHFA still lists the deal on its 2026-09-21 award report, which excludes developments with 8609s issued.

next_step: Watch for 8609 issuance and any opening announcement or lease-up figures.

background.text: The site was bought from RTD; the developers said it took three years and multiple versions of the plan, with support from the City of Aurora's Housing and Community Services Department, to reach groundbreaking.
The Aurora Housing Authority partnership provides a property tax abatement (structure, such as housing authority ownership, not described publicly).
BWE closed the loan in under 90 days in spring 2023; Aurora issued the building permit in April 2023, after a February 2023 revision switching the foundation from footings to drilled piers.
Aurora permit data show 2026 damage-repair permits filed under Mission Rock Sable Station, indicating the building is in operation (inferred).
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2022 Round One or Round Two competitive application narratives; it was a rolling 4% bond deal only.

CHFA's 4% award report says it leaves out developments whose IRS Form 8609s have been issued; this deal is still listed on the 2026-09-21 report, so 8609s had not been issued by then (inferred from the report's note).
